trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (approx. €14, ~30 min). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Once settled, take a relaxed walk to the nearby Piazza Navona — a stunning baroque square that is completely free to explore. Admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and soak in the street art atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the historic centro storico neighborhood. Visit the iconic Trevi Fountain (free) at dusk when the crowds begin to thin and the lighting is magical. Toss a coin and make a wish.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick espresso and cornetto at a bar near Roma Termini for about €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap supplì (fried rice ball) or pizza al taglio from a local bakery near Termini for €3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pizzarium-style street food or a local trattoria near Piazza Navona. Try cacio e pepe pasta or a margherita pizza for €8–12. Look for fixed-price 'menu del giorno' deals.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Use the evening to orient yourself and get comfortable with the neighborhood. Validate your train ticket before boarding. Keep cash handy as many small vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online in advance to skip the line (€20 online vs. longer waits at the door). Arrive early around 9:00 AM for smaller crowds. Marvel at Michelangelo's ceiling and the Gallery of Maps. St. Peter's Basilica entry is FREE — climb to the dome for €8 (stairs) for panoramic views of Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber River and walk to Castel Sant'Angelo (€15 entry), the ancient mausoleum-turned-fortress with incredible rooftop views. Alternatively, walk the scenic Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge lined with angel sculptures for free. Explore the Prati neighborhood nearby, known for affordable local eateries away from tourist traps.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Trastevere, Rome's charming bohemian neighborhood. Wander cobblestone streets, peek into the beautiful Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free), and enjoy the lively evening atmosphere with locals.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and cornetto at a local bar near the hotel — budget €2–3. Avoid sitting down to keep costs low.
meals.lunch: Grab a panino or pizza al taglio near the Vatican for €4–6. Avoid restaurants directly on Vatican Square as they are overpriced.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Trastevere — try Da Enzo al 29 or similar local trattoria. Cacio e pepe or carbonara with house wine for €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Vatican tickets at least a few days in advance, especially in June (peak season). Dress modestly for the Vatican — shoulders and knees must be covered. Bring a refillable water bottle as Rome has free drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill (combined ticket with the Colosseum ~€18, valid 2 days). Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire — the Via Sacra, Temple of Saturn, and Arch of Titus. Palatine Hill offers sweeping views over the Forum and is included in the ticket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use the combined ticket to visit the Colosseum in the afternoon when morning tour groups begin to leave. Book a timed entry online in advance. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the iconic amphitheater. Afterward, walk to the Circus Maximus (free) — the ancient chariot racing stadium.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Aventine Hill for a hidden gem: look through the Knights of Malta keyhole (free) for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Then relax in the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with sunset views over Rome.

meals.breakfast: Bar near the hotel — espresso and pastry for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local alimentari (deli) near the Forum — buy bread, cheese, and cured meats for €5–7 and eat on Palatine Hill.
meals.dinner: Head to Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's culinary heart. Try Flavio al Velavevodetto or a local osteria for authentic Roman cuisine — coda alla vaccinara or offal dishes for €10–14.

day_by_day.notes: June can be hot — bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. The Roman Forum is largely outdoors so plan accordingly. The Colosseum combined ticket is excellent value and covers multiple sites. Testaccio is a locals' neighborhood with some of Rome's best and most affordable food.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings. Entry is €15 but MUST be booked in advance (timed 2-hour slots). Arrive at the 9:00 AM slot. The gallery is set within the beautiful Villa Borghese park.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, spend time in the vast Villa Borghese park (free). Rent a rowboat on the lake (€3–5/hour) or simply relax on the grass. Walk down Via Veneto — the glamorous boulevard made famous by Fellini's La Dolce Vita. Visit the eerie Capuchin Crypt beneath Santa Maria della Concezione church (€8.50) — a macabre art installation made from monks' bones.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Spanish Steps (free) as the sun sets — 135 steps leading to the Trinità dei Monti church. The surrounding Piazza di Spagna area is lively in the evening. Window shop along Via Condotti (Rome's luxury shopping street) for free.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and pastry at a local bar — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park. Buy supplies from a nearby supermarket (Conad or Carrefour) for €5–8.
meals.dinner: Find a budget-friendly restaurant near the Spanish Steps area — try Ristorante Il Sorpasso or a nearby pizzeria. Budget €10–15 per person. Alternatively, grab street food and gelato for a lighter evening.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery booking is essential — this is non-negotiable as they strictly limit visitors. Book online at galleriaborghese.it weeks in advance during peak season. The park is a great midday escape from the heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pantheon (free or small entry fee — check current policy). One of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings, its oculus ceiling is breathtaking. Arrive early to beat crowds. Nearby, visit Sant'Ignazio di Loyola church (free) with its stunning trompe-l'oeil ceiling — a hidden gem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Campo de' Fiori, Rome's lively market square (market runs until ~2:00 PM, free to browse). Buy fresh seasonal fruit, local cheeses, or street food. Afterward, visit the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — walk along Via del Portico d'Ottavia past ancient ruins integrated into the urban fabric. The Great Synagogue has a museum (€12) for those interested.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere or explore Pigneto neighborhood — a hip, artsy area popular with young Romans. Street art, independent bars, and a relaxed vibe. Great for an authentic Roman evening experience away from tourists.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and cornetto at a local bar — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat at Campo de' Fiori — grab supplì, porchetta sandwich, or fresh fruit from market stalls for €4–7.
meals.dinner: Try a local osteria in Trastevere or Pigneto. Look for fixed-price dinner menus (€12–15 including pasta, main, and house wine). Finish with artisanal gelato from a reputable gelateria (€2.50–4).

day_by_day.notes: The Campo de' Fiori market is best visited before noon. Always look for gelato shops that display natural colors and keep gelato in covered metal containers — these are signs of authentic, quality gelato. Avoid places with towering, brightly colored mounds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Ostia Antica — Rome's ancient port city, far less visited than Pompeii but equally impressive. Take the Metro Line B to Laurentina, then the train to Ostia Antica (total ~45 min, covered by standard Roma transport ticket €1.50). Entry is €12. Explore remarkably preserved mosaics, bathhouses, theaters, and apartment buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome by mid-afternoon. Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) — the world's oldest public museums, housing Marcus Aurelius's original bronze equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning views over the Roman Forum from the terrace. The Capitoline Hill itself (Piazza del Campidoglio, designed by Michelangelo) is free.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening revisiting your favorite spot or neighborhood. Consider attending a free outdoor concert or event — Rome has many free cultural events in summer. Check local listings at turismoroma.it.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and pastry at a local bar — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a local supermarket or deli to eat at Ostia Antica (there is a café on-site but it's overpriced). Budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your penultimate night — try a sit-down dinner at a well-reviewed local trattoria. Budget €15–20 per person for a full meal with wine. Testaccio or Trastevere offer the best value.

day_by_day.notes: Ostia Antica is highly recommended for art and history lovers and is far less crowded than most Rome attractions. Wear comfortable shoes as the site is large and mostly outdoors. The Capitoline Museums are best in the afternoon when morning tour groups have left.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit any missed sites or simply enjoy a slow Italian breakfast at a neighborhood bar. Visit the Mercato Testaccio (open until 2:00 PM) — one of Rome's best covered food markets. Sample local cheeses, cured meats, fresh pasta, and Roman street food. A great place to pick up affordable food souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute sightseeing — walk across Rome's bridges over the Tiber for beautiful views. Visit any free churches you may have missed: San Luigi dei Francesi (free, houses three Caravaggio paintings), Santa Maria Maggiore (free), or San Clemente (€10, with remarkable underground layers of Roman history). Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure time, head to the airport via Leonardo Express from Roma Termini. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight. Grab a final espresso at the airport — a fitting farewell to Rome.

meals.breakfast: Final Italian breakfast at a local bar — espresso and cornetto for €2–3. Savor it!
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercato Testaccio — graze on market food for €6–10. Try supplì, trapizzino (pizza pocket sandwiches), or fresh pasta.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a light bite near Termini before departure. Budget €8–12.

day_by_day.notes: San Luigi dei Francesi is a must for art lovers — Caravaggio's three paintings of Saint Matthew are world-class and completely free. Buy any food souvenirs (pasta, olive oil, dried porcini) at supermarkets rather than tourist shops for much better prices. Keep your transport ticket for the airport journey.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use the time to clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, freshen up, and orient yourself to the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the nearby beachfront promenade to shake off jet lag. Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort, grab a gelato from a local gelateria, and get your bearings. Visit a nearby piazza or park to relax and soak in the Roman atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner close to the hotel. Explore a neighborhood trattoria for classic Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or carbonara. End the night with a short evening walk along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Skipped (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light airport or transit snack — grab a panino or tramezzino upon landing
meals.dinner: Neighborhood trattoria near the resort — budget €20–35 per person for pasta, house wine, and dessert (try Ristorante da Mario or similar local spot)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — resist the urge to over-plan. Confirm all booking confirmations for upcoming experiences and check Vatican Museum tickets if not already pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Experience — Head into central Rome early to visit Rome's most beloved food market. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino, fresh produce, and local street food. Arrive by 9:00 AM for the freshest selection and fewest crowds. Chat with vendors and pick up snacks for later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit — After the market, walk or take a short taxi to the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Spend the afternoon exploring the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. The combination ticket covers both sites. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water — it's an expansive open-air site.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Make your way to Trastevere for a guided food and wine evening walk through the cobblestone streets. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla giudia, local wines, and more. This is one of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhoods after dark.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick espresso and cornetto at a local bar near the resort (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Snack generously at Testaccio Market — budget €10–15 for market tastings (porchetta, cheese, olives)
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk tastings, or supplement with a sit-down meal at a Trastevere osteria (€25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Trastevere Evening Walk in advance as spots fill quickly. Testaccio Market closes around 2:00 PM, so arrive early. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover significant ground today.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) with pre-booked skip-the-line tickets to beat the crowds. Spend the morning exploring one of the world's greatest art collections — the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Allow 3–4 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) and climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome (€8). Explore Castel Sant'Angelo nearby. Cross the Tiber and wander through the Prati neighborhood — a great area for window shopping and authentic Roman lunch spots.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and explore the Prati or Trastevere neighborhood for dinner. Enjoy a slower evening — aperitivo hour (Aperol Spritz or Negroni) at a bar around 6:30 PM followed by a proper sit-down dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early espresso and pastry at a bar near the Vatican (€3–5) — eat before entering the museums
meals.lunch: Trattoria in Prati neighborhood near the Vatican — try Il Sorpasso or similar for Roman classics (€20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Aperitivo at a wine bar followed by dinner at a mid-range Trastevere restaurant — budget €30–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be pre-booked — same-day queues can be 2–3 hours. Dress code required for St. Peter's Basilica (covered shoulders and knees). The Sistine Chapel is no-photography — respect the rules.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour — Book the mandatory timed-entry ticket in advance (the gallery limits visitors strictly). Spend 2 hours discovering Bernini's stunning baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. This intimate villa setting is one of Rome's most rewarding art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Borghese Gallery, take a relaxing walk through the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's central park. Rent a rowboat on the lake, enjoy a picnic, or simply stroll. Head down the Spanish Steps to the Trevi Fountain and Pantheon area for classic Rome sightseeing. Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain and explore the Pantheon interior (free or small entry fee).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the lively Campo de' Fiori or Piazza Navona area. Explore the historic center at night when it's beautifully lit. Enjoy a post-dinner gelato from a reputable gelateria (look for 'artigianale' signs).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near the resort before heading out
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up supplies from a nearby deli or alimentari (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Osteria near Campo de' Fiori or Piazza Navona — budget €30–40 per person for antipasto, pasta, and wine

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance — book immediately. Entry is strictly timed (2-hour slots). The gallery only allows 360 visitors at a time. Arrive 15 minutes early. Combine with Villa Borghese for a perfect half-day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Ghetto and Aventine Hill — Visit the ancient Jewish Ghetto, one of Rome's oldest neighborhoods, and see the stunning Portico d'Ottavia ruins. Walk up Aventine Hill to the famous Knights of Malta keyhole (peek through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome) and the peaceful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Testaccio neighborhood (complementing the earlier market visit) for a deeper cultural afternoon. Visit the MACRO Testaccio contemporary art space or explore the Pyramid of Cestius — an unexpected ancient Egyptian-style pyramid right in Rome. Browse the neighborhood's street art and authentic local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour in Testaccio or Ostiense — this is where Romans actually go out. Try a craft cocktail bar or an enoteca (wine bar). Dinner at a beloved local restaurant in Testaccio — the neighborhood is famous for traditional Roman cuisine including offal dishes, but there are plenty of non-offal options too.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and cornetto at a local bar in the Jewish Ghetto area (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Jewish-Roman cuisine lunch in the Ghetto — try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes) and baccalà at a local restaurant (€20–30)
meals.dinner: Testaccio trattoria — try Flavio al Velavevodetto or similar for authentic Roman cuisine (€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Friday evening in Testaccio and Ostiense is lively — Romans head out for the weekend. The Orange Garden on Aventine Hill offers one of the best free panoramic views in Rome. Best visited in the morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip option or deeper neighborhood exploration — Take the train to Ostia Antica (30 minutes from Rome), the remarkably preserved ancient port city of Rome. Far less crowded than Pompeii, it offers an authentic glimpse into Roman daily life with mosaics, temples, and a complete ancient theater. Alternatively, explore the Appian Way by bike for a morning of ancient history and countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome and visit the Palazzo Altemps or Palazzo Massimo alle Terme (National Roman Museum) — two world-class art and sculpture museums that are often overlooked by tourists. The collections include stunning ancient Roman sculptures, frescoes, and mosaics at a very reasonable entry price.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a special Saturday dinner — treat yourself to a slightly upscale Roman restaurant experience. Explore the Pigneto or Prati neighborhood for a more local Saturday night atmosphere. End with a nightcap at a rooftop bar for city views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before catching the train to Ostia Antica
meals.lunch: Packed picnic or simple café lunch at Ostia Antica (limited options on-site, so bring snacks) — budget €10–15
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated Saturday dinner at a well-reviewed Roman restaurant — budget €40–55 per person for a multi-course meal with wine

day_by_day.notes: Ostia Antica trains depart from Porta San Paolo station (connected to Piramide Metro stop). A combined ticket covers the archaeological site. Bring sunscreen and water — it's largely open-air. Book Saturday dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favorite neighborhood or piazza for a slow, unhurried farewell. Sunday morning in Rome is magical — the streets are quiet, the churches are open for mass (beautiful to observe), and the light is golden. Visit a local Sunday market like Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (open until 2:00 PM) for souvenirs and local crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping for food souvenirs — pick up quality olive oil, dried pasta, local wine, or artisan chocolates from a good deli or specialty shop. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Enjoy a final Roman espresso standing at the bar — the authentic Italian way.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — depending on your flight time, either head to the airport or enjoy one last simple dinner near the hotel. A final plate of pasta and a glass of wine to close out a perfect Roman week.

meals.breakfast: Slow Sunday breakfast at a café — cappuccino and a proper Italian breakfast spread (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a trattoria or from the Porta Portese market area — budget €15–20
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner near the resort or airport area — keep it simple and nostalgic (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese flea market runs every Sunday from 7:00 AM to 2:00 PM — arrive early for the best finds. Allow extra time for airport transfer on Sunday as traffic patterns differ. Keep one change of clothes accessible for the journey home. Buon viaggio!

day_by_day.afternoon: Settle In & Neighborhood Stroll — After check-in, take a leisurely orientation walk around the resort's surroundings. Visit a nearby enoteca for a curated wine tasting of Roman DOC whites and Lazio reds to ease into the Roman pace of life.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit — As crowds thin at golden hour, explore the ancient heart of the Roman Empire with a private guide. The warm June light transforms the ruins into something truly cinematic. End with a scenic walk back toward the resort.

meals.breakfast: Onboard or at the airport — no hotel breakfast on Day 1
meals.lunch: Il Pagliaccio (2 Michelin stars) — arrive after check-in for a late lunch tasting menu featuring refined Roman ingredients; reserve ahead
meals.dinner: Aroma Restaurant at Palazzo Manfredi — rooftop dining with an unobstructed view of the Colosseum; indulge in the seasonal degustation menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Pre-book the Palatine Hill sunset private tour (skip-the-line entry essential in June). Confirm late check-in with the resort. Dress code at Aroma is smart elegant.

The tour culminates in an intimate, unhurried experience of Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — After the museums, cross into St. Peter's Square and explore the Basilica with your guide. Climb to the top of Michelangelo's dome for panoramic views over Rome. Afterward, enjoy a slow espresso at a historic café in the Prati neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — As the sun sets, cross the Tiber into Trastevere for a curated food and wine evening walk through cobblestone streets. Sample supplì, artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and local wines with a knowledgeable culinary guide.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a full spread of pastries, fruit, eggs, and Italian cold cuts on the terrace
meals.lunch: Ristorante Il Sorpasso (Prati) — a stylish all-day eatery near the Vatican; enjoy Roman classics like cacio e pepe and artichoke salad with a glass of natural wine
meals.dinner: Grazia & Graziella (Trastevere) — intimate trattoria with an outstanding seasonal menu; conclude the evening walk here for a full sit-down dinner with local Frascati wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-opening Vatican access must be booked weeks in advance through a licensed tour operator. Wear comfortable shoes for the full day of walking. The Trastevere walk is best enjoyed at a relaxed pace — allow 3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour — Begin with a private guided tour of the Borghese Gallery, one of Rome's most intimate and extraordinary museums. Marvel at Bernini's baroque sculptural masterpieces and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. Entry is strictly timed — your guide will handle all logistics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincian Hill — After the gallery, stroll through the lush Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax in the shade. Walk up to the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Private Rooftop Aperitivo & Fine Dining — Return to central Rome for a sunset aperitivo on a private rooftop terrace. Then dine at a top-tier Roman restaurant for a full evening of refined Italian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — seasonal fruit, cornetti freschi, cappuccino, and eggs cooked to order on the resort terrace
meals.lunch: Caffè delle Arti (inside the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna near Villa Borghese) — elegant garden café serving refined Italian plates; perfect after the gallery
meals.dinner: La Pergola at Rome Cavalieri (3 Michelin stars) — Rome's pinnacle of fine dining; Chef Heinz Beck's legendary tasting menu with an extraordinary 60,000-bottle wine cellar; reserve months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery entry is capped at 360 visitors per session — booking private access is essential. La Pergola requires a formal dress code (jacket for gentlemen). A private car is recommended for the La Pergola transfer as it is located on Monte Mario.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Experience — Immerse yourself in Rome's most authentic food market, where locals have shopped for generations. With a culinary expert guide, sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, fresh ricotta, seasonal produce, and street food. Learn the stories behind each vendor and product.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Pasta & Roman Cuisine Cooking Class — Following the market, head to a private kitchen studio where a Michelin-trained chef leads an exclusive hands-on cooking class. Craft fresh pasta (tonnarelli cacio e pepe, rigatoni all'amatriciana) and a traditional Roman dessert, then sit down to eat your creations.
day_by_day.evening: Aventine Hill & Knights of Malta Keyhole — Take a sunset walk up the Aventine Hill to the famous Knights of Malta keyhole, where a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome awaits. Stroll through the tranquil Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) as the city glows below.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — indulge in a Roman-style spread with fresh cornetti, prosciutto, local honey, and barista-made espresso
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as your midday meal — a full multi-course Roman lunch prepared by you and your private chef
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — beloved Roman institution carved into Monte dei Cocci; iconic cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara in a warm, convivial atmosphere; request a private dining area

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is liveliest before noon — an early start is recommended. The cooking class can be arranged at a private villa or studio kitchen for a truly exclusive experience. Aventine Hill is a short taxi ride from Testaccio.

day_by_day.morning: Capitoline Museums Private Tour — Explore the world's oldest public museums with a private art historian guide. Admire the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and breathtaking views over the Roman Forum from the terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pantheon & Historic Center Exploration — Walk to the perfectly preserved Pantheon for a guided visit, then wander the historic center: Piazza Navona, Campo de' Fiori, and hidden Renaissance courtyards. Stop at a historic pasticceria for a traditional gelato or granita.
day_by_day.evening: Private Illuminated Rome Night Tour — As darkness falls and monuments are dramatically lit, take a private chauffeured tour of Rome by night: Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps, Colosseum, and Piazza Venezia. End with a nightcap at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — full resort breakfast with a focus on fresh pastries, seasonal fruit platters, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Ristorante Pierluigi (Campo de' Fiori area) — elegant seafood-forward Roman cuisine in a beautiful piazza setting; try the sea bass carpaccio and lobster spaghetti
meals.dinner: Imàgo at Hotel Hassler (rooftop, Spanish Steps) — panoramic Roman skyline views with an inventive modern Italian tasting menu and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book Capitoline Museums private access in advance. The night tour is best arranged with a luxury tour operator providing a Mercedes van or similar. Trevi Fountain is most magical after midnight — consider a brief return later in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Castel Gandolfo & Castelli Romani — A private chauffeured excursion to the Castelli Romani hills south of Rome. Visit the Papal Palace gardens at Castel Gandolfo (now open to the public), explore the volcanic lake views, and breathe in the cooler hill air — a perfect contrast to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Frascati Wine Estate Visit — Stop at a prestigious Frascati wine estate in the Castelli Romani for an exclusive private cellar tour and guided tasting of Frascati Superiore DOCG whites paired with local cheeses, cured meats, and olive oils. Return to Rome by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Private Chef Dinner Experience — For a truly memorable final full evening, arrange a private chef dinner at a rented palazzo or rooftop terrace in central Rome. A renowned Roman chef prepares a bespoke multi-course menu using market-fresh ingredients, with a sommelier pairing each course.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — leisurely morning meal before the day trip departure; enjoy pastries, yogurt, and espresso on the terrace
meals.lunch: Antico Ristorante Pagnanelli (Castel Gandolfo) — a historic lakeside restaurant with panoramic views of Lago Albano; classic Roman-Castelli cuisine with fresh lake fish and local wines
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner experience — fully customized menu; coordinate with a luxury concierge service such as Rome's top culinary agencies for chef and venue booking

day_by_day.notes: The Castel Gandolfo Papal gardens require advance booking. Depart by 9:00 AM to make the most of the day. The private chef dinner should be arranged at least 2 weeks in advance through the hotel concierge — specify dietary preferences and wine preferences for a fully tailored experience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Final Morning & Spa — Enjoy a slow, indulgent final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Treat yourself to a signature spa treatment — a Roman-inspired thermal ritual or a deep-tissue massage — followed by a long, unhurried breakfast overlooking the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Wander & Personal Shopping — Head into the city for a final afternoon of personal exploration. Browse the luxury boutiques along Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi), visit a high-end antique dealer near Campo de' Fiori for a unique art piece to bring home, or simply sit at a historic café and soak in the Roman atmosphere one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparation — Enjoy a memorable farewell dinner before returning to the resort to pack and prepare for departure. The hotel concierge arranges a private chauffeur for the airport transfer.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — the full spread, enjoyed slowly: eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit, and a final perfect cappuccino
meals.lunch: Caffè Greco (Via Condotti) — Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), frequented by Keats, Goethe, and Casanova; enjoy a light lunch of tramezzini, salads, and a glass of Prosecco in historic surroundings
meals.dinner: Enoteca La Torre at Villa Laetitia — elegant, art-filled restaurant on the banks of the Tiber; Chef Domenico Stile's creative Italian cuisine with an extraordinary wine selection; the perfect farewell to Rome

day_by_day.notes: Schedule the spa in advance — morning slots on the final day are popular. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge the night before (allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights). Via Condotti boutiques open around 10:00 AM. Luggage storage can be arranged at the resort while you enjoy your final afternoon.
